narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

A warm day is set to climb toward a high of 30°C (86°F), while the sky begins early Mostly cloudy, clears to Mostly clear by midday and shifts to Partly cloudy in the evening. thunder possible, peaking this evening. The wind will be northeasterly overnight, turning southwest by midday, with gusts up to 37 km/h (20 kt) ashore. UV reaches a peak index of 9.1. Air quality is forecast at AQI 81 from the model estimate. As of 06:01, reports through 04:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 23°C (73°F); low so far 21°C (70°F); peak sustained 6 km/h (3 kt); sky mostly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

NEXT THREE DAYS will see temperatures and winds much the same through Sunday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Friday will be Partly cloudy with rain, 100% probability, high between 28°C (82°F) and 30°C (86°F). Saturday will be Mostly cloudy with rain, 100% probability, high between 28°C (82°F) and 30°C (86°F). Sunday will be Mostly cloudy with rain, 100% probability, high between 29°C (84°F) and 30°C (86°F). The call gives a rain amount of 3.4 mm (0.13 in) for Sunday and a peak gust of 28 km/h (15 kt). RECORD notes the best rain record for Day+3 belongs to ECMWF.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE values rise sharply, with GFS at 1030 J/kg, ECMWF 1700 J/kg, ICON 1660 J/kg, UKMO 3730 J/kg and Best Match 1660 J/kg, peaking around 20:00. This supports thunder possible, peaking this evening, and the risk of sudden gusts well above the forecast 37 km/h (20 kt). KMD’s bulletin mentions light showers and thunderstorms over a few places tonight, reinforcing the threat.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Winam Gulf wind will be east-northeasterly overnight at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 9 km/h (5 kt), then turn southwesterly by midday at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 18 km/h (10 kt), and increase to 13 km/h (7 kt) gusting 20 km/h (11 kt) into the evening, with a peak gust of 28 km/h (15 kt). Thunder possible this evening raises the chance of gusts exceeding the forecast.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1010 hPa) and highest toward the northeast (1016 hPa) – a 6 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the south – a large-scale feature building in that direction, though the speed is unknown. Pressure overhead is near-steady. BASIN PRESSURE: today’s mean sea-level pressure sits between 1014.1 and 1016.3 hPa; near-steady over three days (-1.4 hPa). The call notes a pressure trend of +0.4 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

REVIEW finds that at Day+0 no model is meaningfully better than the others, and Best Match slightly under-forecasts daytime highs and peak wind. RECORD shows the best rain record for Day+0 belongs to GFS, yet GFS does not see this location’s thunderstorms coming, putting it on the wrong side of its own record. The CALL’s high of 30°C (86°F) matches the upper end of model ranges (28-30°C [82-86°F]) and its peak gust of 37 km/h (20 kt) aligns with the Best Match gust of 38.2 km/h (21 kt). KMD forecasts a max of 29°C (84°F) and light showers, slightly cooler than the CALL but consistent on rain. DATA SUFFICIENCY notes 68 checks for Day+0, giving a settled picture despite uneven model coverage.
